6061-vs-7075-cnc-aluminum.heading: 6061 vs 7075 aluminum for CNC parts
6061-vs-7075-cnc-aluminum.description: Compare 6061 and 7075 by strength, stiffness, temper, stock form, joining and anodized fit, with product conditions beside the data.
6061-vs-7075-cnc-aluminum.intro: Compare 6061 vs 7075 aluminum against the requirement that limits the finished part. The specified 6061 condition is a useful starting point when it meets the loads, exposure and finish; 7075 is worth considering where a restricted section needs more strength. A thin cover that bends may benefit more from a shorter span or a rib than from an alloy change.
6061-vs-7075-cnc-aluminum.summary: Choose the alloy around the load, geometry, temper and finished interfaces.
6061-vs-7075-cnc-aluminum.reader_question: When does 7075 solve a CNC part problem that 6061 cannot, and what trade-offs come with it?

sections.title: Which requirement drives the alloy choice?
sections.html:
6061 vs 7075 material selection should start with the limiting requirement. Aluminum bracket strength around a loaded pin bore presents a different problem from deflection of a broad enclosure lid. The bracket may need more resistance to yielding around the bore. The lid may need a stiffer section so it stays flat between screws. Selecting the higher strength alloy helps only if strength governs the design.

Design priority60617075
Loaded section with little room to growSuitable where the specified condition meets the calculated requirement.Worth comparing when higher strength is needed in the available section.
Broad wall or cover that deflectsSpan, thickness and support strongly affect the result.Its higher strength brings a much smaller change in elastic stiffness.
Exposure and joiningOften considered for corrosion resistance and welded construction.Temper, protection and sustained stress deserve closer review; welding assumptions change.
Anodized appearanceAn appearance sample still needs the actual alloy and preparation.Can be anodized, with its own visual reference and dimensional route.

The material data must describe the product being purchased. Kaiser publishes separate sheets for 6061 sheet, coil and plate and 7075 rod and bar. A typical brochure value helps explain a choice; the applicable product specification establishes the purchase requirement.

sections.title: Why more strength may leave a cover just as flexible
sections.html:
In a 6061 vs 7075 strength comparison, yield strength describes when permanent deformation begins under the relevant load. Elastic modulus answers the 6061 vs 7075 stiffness question: how much the part deforms elastically before that point. A stronger bracket can carry a higher stress while an otherwise identical cover still bends by a similar amount.

Kaiser's 6061 rod and bar sheet gives typical T6/T651 yield strength of 276 MPa and modulus of 68.3 GPa. Its 7075 rod and bar sheet gives 503 MPa and 71.0 GPa for T6/T651. These are typical brochure properties, not guaranteed design allowables or minimum purchasing values.

Read both ratios before changing the design

Those values give a yield-strength ratio of 503 / 276 ≈ 1.82 and a modulus ratio of 71.0 / 68.3 ≈ 1.04. For an illustrative elastic calculation in which geometry, loading and support remain identical and deflection varies inversely with modulus, a hypothetical 1.00 mm deflection would become about 1.00 × 68.3 / 71.0 = 0.96 mm. That example isolates the material effect; it predicts no particular enclosure's performance.

If that small change leaves the lid outside its deflection requirement, the next design review concerns its unsupported span, wall section, ribs or screw arrangement. Each option must still leave room for the contents and mating cover. A loaded bore may lead to a different conclusion because the stress in its remaining ligament, rather than bending of a broad panel, sets the requirement.

sections.title: Buy the condition used in the comparison
sections.html:
For a 6061 T6 vs 7075 T6 comparison, identify the aluminum stock product form, applicable size range and purchasing standard. Those details and the temper determine which properties apply; a drawing that says only 7075 leaves them unresolved. A rod-and-bar comparison cannot establish every requirement for a thick plate.

T651 stress relieved aluminum includes stress relief by stretching, as described in BIKAR's temper information. Its requirements depend on the product form. A switch from T6 therefore needs approval against the drawing, as any other material change does.

Kaiser's 7075 data distinguish T6/T651 from T73/T7351. For a 7075 T73 corrosion resistance review, those data describe improved stress-corrosion resistance with lower typical strength. The environment and sustained loading determine whether that trade-off suits the part. Its 7075 sheet, coil and plate data provide the corresponding product-family reference. The order then needs the applicable specification and material records for the stock actually used.

Check the basis of the material comparison

A housing quote may use plate while a sleeve quote uses round bar. Check the quoted thickness or diameter range and the property direction where the specification distinguishes it. A typical specimen value does not establish the minimum strength of every stock size.

The 6061 and 7075 rod-and-bar sheets used above label their mechanical data as typical. Use those values to understand the design question, then obtain the applicable purchasing limits for the proposed stock. Request a named alternative if the quoted condition differs from the released drawing.

sections.title: An enclosure needs several kinds of surface
sections.html:
In a pocketed enclosure, the cavity wall may mainly protect the contents, a mounting face may locate the housing, and the lid rim may control closure. Treating every surface as equally loaded can lead to an expensive alloy choice while leaving the fit problem unresolved.

In the pocketed enclosure study, the visible geometry and holding arrangements help identify locating faces. The photographs do not identify the alloy. For a new design, distinguish a press-fit bore from a sliding or clearance opening on the drawing.

Removing the pocket also changes support during machining. Stock condition, the remaining sections and the measurement state affect whether the released part meets its flatness requirement. The enclosure design guide follows those decisions through pocket access, wall support and lid fit.

sections.title: Follow the force through the working section
sections.html:
A bracket's outside dimensions say little about the stress in a narrow ligament beside a bore. Trace the force from the pin or fastener into the surrounding section and on to the mounting face. That identifies the region where a higher strength material might help.

The same review needs the joint details. A threaded connection depends on engagement, thread geometry, mating material and assembly load. A pin connection brings bearing contact and fit into the calculation. The multi-feature part examples show how faces and holes can serve different roles on one component; the drawing example connects a selected feature to its inspection result.

For a billet intake manifold, flange alignment, internal access and any split joint add requirements that a strength comparison cannot settle. The material belongs to that complete component definition, with operating tests identified separately.

sections.title: Exposure and joining can change the preferred alloy
sections.html:
To compare corrosion resistance in 6061 and 7075 aluminum, start with the moisture, chemicals and sustained loads the part will see in service. Check the mating metals and whether the joint makes electrical contact, particularly where bare aluminum meets another metal. If the design calls for welding, identify the welding process and assess it for the specified alloy and temper.

Hydro's 6061 technical sheet discusses its corrosion resistance and welding uses, including the reduced strength that welding can produce in the T6 weld region. A welded design therefore needs the joint's own design and qualification.

Changing that design to 7075 also changes the joining assessment. Conventional fusion welding needs a separate suitability review; the earlier 6061 welding assumptions cannot carry across automatically. In a bolted version, fit, preload and the local corrosion arrangement become part of the joint specification.

sections.title: The assembly receives the anodized dimensions
sections.html:
6061 vs 7075 anodizing comparisons need appearance samples for the actual alloy and preparation. An anodized aluminum fit allowance also needs the selected process and the final working dimensions. A black sample made from one alloy is an incomplete acceptance reference for another. The sample should represent the intended material, preparation and treatment.

Anodizing converts the surface to oxide, with part of that oxide extending beyond the original surface. The Aluminum Anodizers Council FAQ explains process-dependent growth and different nominal relationships for Type II and hardcoat. The actual route determines the allowance needed on a precision interface.

A bore that locates a pin needs a finished size, while its chamfer and adjacent shoulder need a clear treatment boundary. The material and finish guide explains how to connect those final dimensions to coating, masking and inspection.

sections.title: Stock and support still govern distortion
sections.html:
Aluminum machining distortion is a concern when a deep asymmetric pocket leaves a new balance of support. Stress relieved plate stock can be part of the route, while geometry, fixture loads and the operation sequence still need review against the required shape after release.

The two-operation milling study illustrates the locating problem when a component is repositioned. Features made in separate setups must keep their intended relationship once the holding forces are removed.

A flatness result needs a stated measurement condition. A thin panel measured free can differ from the same panel restrained at its screw positions. The approved drawing and quotation should retain the required condition through any proposed material or process change.

sections.title: Compare finished designs with the same requirements
sections.html:
Compare 6061 vs 7075 machining cost against the same finished drawing where either alloy suits the design. An aluminum enclosure material decision should retain the actual wall, interface, treatment and inspection requirements in that comparison. If 7075 permits a redesigned section, compare the complete approved designs, including any changed machining and finishing work.

Keep the geometry visible in a machinability comparison

A shallow block and a thin enclosure removed from a large blank place different demands on the route. Stock form, removal volume, holding stages, final finish and inspection can matter more to the quotation than the alloy's price per kilogram. The machining cost guide explains these other sources of work.

For a 6061-T6 and 7075-T6 comparison, material data and certificates need to match the ordered product form. An alternative remains a proposal until the responsible designer approves it. The selected alloy and condition then become part of the sample and repeat-order record.

Compare alternatives against the requirement that limits the part
ObservationComparison to makeInformation needed before approval
A cover bends between screwsCompare span, thickness and support as well as elastic modulus.The allowed deflection and installed support arrangement.
A loaded bracket has little remaining sectionCompare the approved material properties and complete joint design.Load cases, stock condition and the responsible engineering assessment.
The 7075 quote is higherCompare the same finished drawing, records, treatment and inspection scope.Stock form, blank size and changed holding or finishing work.
A different temper is available soonerReview that exact condition against the design and finish.The proposed specification and substitution approval.

For a deep enclosure, ask whether the alternative changes the blank thickness, roughing sequence or support during the final cuts. A lower material price can be outweighed by extra stock removal or a different finishing route. Record the approved alternative against the drawing revision so the next order does not reopen the comparison.

If the limiting feature is a wall or pocket, compare support and permitted geometry changes in the enclosure wall and pocket review before settling on an alloy change.

sections.title: What to send when the alloy is undecided
sections.html:
If the alloy is undecided, explain what is limiting the design: a load in a small section, a deflection limit, a wet environment, a welding requirement or an appearance target. Include the mating interfaces and any constraints on changing the geometry.

Alongside the current model and drawing, the review needs the proposed grade and temper, product form, initial and repeat quantities, final treatment and required records. Any substitute should appear as a named alternative with an approver, so a quotation assumption does not become an accidental production requirement.

LZZ's listed aluminum options include 6061, 7075 and 2024, subject to the part and material review. The aluminum machining page provides the entry point for discussing that scope.

sections.title: What the alloy choice leaves open
sections.html:
Does 7075 allow a tighter tolerance?

A tolerance belongs to a feature and its finished condition. Stock, geometry, holding, sequence, treatment and measurement determine the route for meeting it. The alloy name supplies no general tolerance guarantee.

What does the material certificate establish?

It identifies the material and stated compliance or results within its scope. It does not approve the component geometry, assembly strength or finished dimensions.

Can pricing begin before the drawing is released?

A current model, drawing and quantities can support a discussion of alternatives. The quotation should identify assumptions and open decisions. Production then follows the approved material and revision.

material-and-finish-checklist.seoTitle: Materials and finishes for CNC machined parts
material-and-finish-checklist.heading: Materials and finishes for CNC machined parts
material-and-finish-checklist.description: Connect exact material grades, surface treatments, masking and appearance to final fits and the records needed to accept a CNC part.
material-and-finish-checklist.intro: A locating bore, an electrical contact and a visible cover can need different treatments on the same CNC machined part. Specify the exact material and service conditions, then follow each working interface through machining, treatment and final inspection.
material-and-finish-checklist.summary: Grade, local treatment, final fit and evidence for accepting the delivered part.
material-and-finish-checklist.reader_question: How do I order the right material and finish without losing the fits or evidence my assembly needs?

sections.title: Start with the duty and the exact material
sections.html:
CNC material and finish selection follows the duty of the part. The material grade and condition for a lightweight cover can differ from those for a current-carrying contact or a chemically exposed fitting, even when the shapes are similar. Loads and temperature matter, as do the mating material, moisture, cleaning chemicals, electrical duty and cleanliness.

For aluminum, the order needs alloy and temper; 6061, 7075 and 2024 do not describe the same design option. Stainless steel such as 304, 316 or 17-4PH needs its condition and any heat treatment. Copper and brass require the full designation and applicable standard. C3600, H62 and C36000 are separate names and cannot be exchanged by shortening or translating them.

For POM, PEEK and PPSU, the exact polymer and inspection condition matter to the fit. Titanium, Inconel, Kovar and Invar likewise need an exact designation and intended use for review. Availability and the material-record scope should be settled before purchasing stock; substitutions need an identified approver.

The 6061 and 7075 comparison follows an aluminum decision in detail. The stainless, copper and brass and engineering-plastics pages describe the corresponding inquiry scope.

sections.title: Give working surfaces and visible surfaces their own requirements
sections.html:
A CNC surface finish specification can assign different requirements to the same enclosure. Cosmetic surface acceptance may concern exterior color, while a fitted bore needs a controlled diameter and a grounding pad needs a specified electrical contact. One blanket finish note leaves these different jobs unresolved.

Deburring, blasting, polishing, anodizing, passivation and plating each need a material-compatible process and an agreed order scope. The drawing should identify the treated region, applicable process specification and revision, thickness requirements where relevant, and any required sequence. An appearance reference then controls the visible result: color, gloss, texture and permitted marks under agreed viewing conditions.

A general treatment can still apply to the whole part if the local exceptions are easy to find. For a small internal surface, a section or named face is more useful than an informal instruction in an email. Machining, finishing and receiving inspection need to be able to point to the same region.

Questions to settle when selecting a finishing route
Route being consideredInterface questionRequirement to carry into the order
Blasting followed by anodizingWhich visible faces need the selected texture, and which fits must remain controlled?Preparation sequence, local exceptions, appearance reference and final dimensions.
Stainless passivationWhich grade, processing condition and verification apply?Named treatment specification and required records for that grade.
Electroless nickel platingHow will deposited material affect bores, threads and shoulders?Required thickness scope, treated areas and final fit checks.
Local polishingDoes the removal change a fitted surface or edge?Permitted region, dimensional limits and a measurable finish requirement.

Specify how roughness and appearance will be accepted as well as naming the process. A blasted enclosure, for example, can have a separately protected lid register. NASA/JSC's anodizing specification discusses preparation and dimensional planning. Agree the route with the finishing supplier under the specification selected for the order.

sections.title: Work backward from the finished fit
sections.html:
Dimensions after surface treatment govern a fit that enters assembly in the treated state. A coating thickness allowance must be reviewed against the actual process and final limits, including growth at the opposing surfaces. A bore accepted before treatment may shrink afterward; a coated outside diameter can grow. Threads, seal tracks and sliding faces can also depend on where the coating ends.

Anodizing forms oxide within and beyond the original surface. The Aluminum Anodizers Council FAQ describes different nominal relationships for Type II and hardcoat, with growth affected by the alloy and process. Total coating thickness and outward growth are separate quantities.

An allowance example with assumed values

Suppose a reviewed process is assumed to produce 10 micrometres of outward growth on each exposed surface. An outside diameter would grow by about 20 micrometres; a bore coated on both sides would lose about 20 micrometres of opening. This arithmetic illustrates opposing surfaces. The assumed value is neither a coating specification nor an instruction to machine a particular size.

The actual allowance needs the process variation, preparation and local geometry. Deep, narrow openings also raise a coverage question. NASA/JSC PRC-5006 discusses hard-anodizing coverage and dimensional planning; its requirements apply when that specification is called out. A critical internal feature may need a masked region, an approved operation afterward or a fully treated fit whose limits the route can meet.

sections.title: Draw the boundary where the treatment stops
sections.html:
Anodizing masking boundaries must resolve the bore, entry chamfer, nearby shoulder and any intersecting opening. Thread gauging after treatment similarly needs the finished connection and permitted processing sequence identified. Leaving those boundaries undefined can move a treatment edge into the working fit.

Threads need the full designation, class, usable depth and final gauging condition. A treated thread, a masked thread and a thread completed after treatment follow different routes. Cutting or chasing after treatment can expose base material, which needs approval where protection or cleanliness is affected.

For a grounding or current-carrying pad, the required contact area and assembled condition belong beside the permitted treatment and mating material. A processing rack mark has a different purpose; its allowed location should preserve the functional and cosmetic regions. If contact resistance forms part of acceptance, it needs its own limits and test responsibility.

The anodizing masking guide compares the available routes for a fitted aluminum feature.

sections.title: A smooth-looking face can still need a roughness result
sections.html:
Machined surface roughness on a sealing face needs its specified parameter and measurement basis. An anodized appearance reference separately describes the visible result under the agreed viewing conditions. Color, gloss and permitted marks cannot replace Ra or Rz, just as one roughness result cannot establish that two panels look alike.

The roughness callout needs its parameter, units, limit, applicable standard and the region to measure. Measurement conditions belong with it where they affect the result. Form and waviness have separate controls. The drawing guide explains those distinctions.

Preparation remains visible through later processing. NASA/JSC's anodizing guidance describes the influence of the starting texture; anodizing should not be relied on to erase milling marks. If the desired appearance requires blasting or polishing first, the sample should represent that sequence on the specified alloy. Retaining the accepted reference and viewing conditions makes later batches easier to judge.

sections.title: The same finish language does not suit every material
sections.html:
Stainless steel

Stainless steel passivation addresses contamination such as free iron under the selected process. Electroplated contact surfaces raise a separate substrate-and-coating question, so a treatment name should stay with the material and interface it describes. Carpenter Technology's guidance describes grade-dependent processing and testing. The order needs the exact grade, condition, treatment standard and required verification, including the sequence around heat treatment. A corrosion test, when required, has its own acceptance scope.

Copper and brass contacts

The substrate and plating are separate requirements. A current-carrying face or thermal contact needs its working area, surface condition and mating arrangement, while a visible exterior can have a different appearance requirement. Material identity and dimensional inspection do not establish an assembled electrical or thermal result.

Engineering plastics

A polymer's measured size can change with temperature and moisture condition. Ensinger's dimensional-stability guidance distinguishes thermal expansion and moisture uptake across materials. For a plastic part inside a metal housing, the service environment and agreed measurement condition make the fit meaningful. The plastic measurement guide covers conditioning and support.

sections.title: Separate a solid polymer from a coated or covered part
sections.html:
Solid PTFE parts contain the specified polymer throughout. Teflon coated metal parts instead have a metal substrate and a separate surface treatment. A covered wheel or roller adds another construction, with a covering that must be retained. Those designs need different material and dimensional definitions.

The Teflon coating collection shows round components and long pieces with repeated holes. On a round part, the outside working surface, bore and mounting faces may have different treatment requirements. On a long part, coating inside the holes can affect the mating connection.

The production definition should therefore give the substrate, coating or covering, treated regions and boundaries, along with required thickness, adhesion and service criteria. Critical sizes need a stated before- or after-treatment condition. A separate covering also needs its retention method defined.

sections.title: Follow one housing interface all the way to acceptance
sections.html:
The pocketed enclosure study shows the cavity and setup. In a new housing of this form, the base may locate the housing, a bore may locate another component and the lid rim may support a seal. Give each of those faces the requirements its function needs.

For the locating bore, begin with the final size and its datum relationship. The treated or masked condition determines the allowance and final check. If machining afterward is proposed, the resulting exposed surface needs an accepted protection requirement. The process-selection guide connects the working faces to holding and cutting stages.

Keep the closure rim distinct from the cavity wall

On the pocketed housing reference, the cavity provides space while the rim and openings can locate or seal. The exterior color says nothing about whether the rim is flat or the bore has the right final fit. The finish proposal needs to carry each requirement through the corresponding preparation, treatment and inspection stage.

sections.title: The delivered surface includes its edges and handling condition
sections.html:
A defined chamfer protects a mating seal differently from an unspecified edge break. The drawing should distinguish edges that need a radius or chamfer, edges whose shape must remain, and internal intersections where loose burrs could reach a passage or working contact.

After finishing, a sliding face can still be scratched by another part in the box. Packing requirements should preserve cosmetic faces, threads and seal regions, with separation and cleanliness appropriate to the specified surface. The packing and shipping guide covers that delivery scope.

If damage or an out-of-limit fit requires polishing, stripping, recoating or touch-up, the disposition needs approval against the drawing. The record should show the permitted work and its effect on final dimensions and appearance. An accepted rework route can then be distinguished from an undocumented change.

sections.title: A certificate and a dimensional report answer different questions
sections.html:
Use material certificate traceability to connect the specified grade and condition to the supplied batch. Surface treatment records should identify the processing route and required results for that material and order. Dimensional inspection records the interfaces in their agreed state, while appearance approval uses the identified reference and viewing conditions. Each document needs the relevant part, revision and batch link.

These requirements affect the quotation. Certificate availability, sampling, test limits and report format should be agreed before production, including any customer or industry documentation requirements. The release decision should retain accepted deviations, rework and outstanding items.

Check the records for an anodized housing bore

For an anodized housing bore, match the material record to the alloy and temper on the drawing and the treatment record to the specified process. Electroless nickel plating and stainless passivation need their corresponding records. A treatment name supplies neither a thickness requirement nor evidence of the final fit.

Start with the delivered part number and revision, then follow the material identification into the processing record and final inspection sheet. If the finisher uses another batch reference, retain the cross-reference. A certificate with the right alloy name but no connection to the supplied lot leaves traceability unresolved.

The bore result should state whether it was measured after treatment or after an approved later sizing operation. Record any separate protection of masked regions, so receiving inspection can compare the finished interface with the drawing.

Settle certificate language, report format and required batch or individual identification during quotation. Identical treatment names can otherwise arrive with different documentation.

sections.title: Decisions to resolve before production
sections.html:
Can coating thickness be subtracted from a bore size?

The allowance depends on the process and on growth at opposing surfaces. For anodizing, outward growth differs from total coating thickness. Preparation, variation and internal coverage also belong in the feature review.

Will anodizing hide a cutter mark?

The preparation and finished texture need an agreement before treatment. If a visible face requires blasting or polishing, its defined area and acceptance reference should represent that route.

Can one certificate cover the finished fit?

Only when its agreed scope includes the relevant final dimensional evidence. A process certificate commonly answers a different question from a fitted-bore measurement.

Can an inquiry start with an open finish choice?

Yes. Send the part function, known environment and working interfaces, with candidate treatments and unresolved choices marked on the current files. Production needs an approved material, treatment route and acceptance conditions.

designing-aluminum-enclosures-for-cnc-ma.seoTitle: Designing aluminum enclosures for CNC machining
designing-aluminum-enclosures-for-cnc-ma.heading: Designing aluminum enclosures for CNC machining
designing-aluminum-enclosures-for-cnc-ma.description: Design a machined aluminum enclosure around lid fit, mounting interfaces, wall support, pocket access, thread depth and final anodized dimensions.
designing-aluminum-enclosures-for-cnc-ma.intro: CNC aluminum enclosure design starts with the lid, board mounts and connector openings in the finished assembly. For a housing machined from solid stock, those locating interfaces establish the datums and fit requirements. Review the surrounding cavity for wall support, corner radii and tool access.
designing-aluminum-enclosures-for-cnc-ma.summary: Connect enclosure fit to pocket geometry, support and the finished condition.
designing-aluminum-enclosures-for-cnc-ma.reader_question: How can I make an aluminum enclosure practical to machine while keeping the lid and internal components aligned?

sections.title: Let the assembly establish the reference surfaces
sections.html:
CNC enclosure datum selection should follow the electronics enclosure interfaces that actually locate the assembly. A board may sit on internal bosses, a connector may locate from the base and a lid may register on a step around the opening. Tight outside dimensions alone cannot establish those relationships. The drawing needs the references that connect each component to the installed housing.

The pocketed aluminum housing shows a cavity, closure rim and floor or side openings. Sections through those regions reveal the material left beneath pockets and around ports. The mating lid needs its own revision, with any gasket, O-ring or conductive contact defined at the actual interface.

A consistent datum scheme lets the machining review consider holding and measurement around the same functional references. Some outside faces may need only general dimensional limits; mounting or closure faces can need local position, flatness or surface controls.

Solid stock, extrusions and folded panels

A finished-box model can conceal the starting form. Milling from solid removes a cavity; machining an extrusion begins with a profile and may add separate end panels; folded construction brings joints and forming into the assembly. An extrusion inquiry therefore also needs the profile and end-panel definitions. A wall recommendation for one construction cannot establish the limit for another.

Check the lid, board and connector in one assembly section

For a hypothetical electronics enclosure, the board sits on internal bosses while a connector passes through a side wall. The connector opening depends on boss height and board position as well as the cutout itself. A drawing that controls the opening only from the outside base can miss the assembled relationship.

Start the tolerance stack from the surface that actually supports the board. Carry it through the board and connector mounting details to the wall opening. Check the same installed arrangement with the lid fitted, including screw heads, cable bends and clearance to internal ribs. The responsible designer selects the permissible accumulated variation.

A lid register tolerance controls the locating relationship while screws retain the cover. An enclosure O-ring groove, where used, must follow the selected seal and approved joint geometry. If a gasket or O-ring seals the joint, its specified compression depends on the selected seal and gland geometry. The Parker O-Ring Handbook provides application-specific design information. Seal selection and enclosure machining should use that approved joint definition.

sections.title: Review the wall at its full height and the corner at full depth
sections.html:
CNC enclosure wall thickness needs to be considered with the full unsupported height. Deep pocket CNC machining also changes cutter reach and holder clearance; a tall uninterrupted wall has less support than a short wall reinforced by bosses at the same thickness. These local details explain why a universal minimum wall thickness is a poor release rule.

Where the assembly leaves room, a shorter unsupported span or material around a boss can improve support. The fixed interfaces should remain clear so a proposed change does not move a lid register, mounting hole or sealing path.

A conventional round cutter leaves a radius in an internal corner. In a geometric example, a 6 mm end mill has a 3 mm radius and cannot produce a smaller corner in an ordinary milling pass. Requiring exactly R3 also leaves that cutter little room to move through the corner. A larger permitted part radius or a smaller tool gives the route another option, subject to depth and reach. This example establishes geometry, not a general minimum radius.

Sandvik Coromant's inside-corner guidance explains the increased engagement as a tool enters a corner. A small cutter that fits a shallow recess can require a much longer projection at the bottom of a deep pocket, where a step or boss may also block the holder.

Make a cost option a controlled geometry change

If the internal corner radius only provides clearance, ask for a price with a larger approved radius. Enclosure corner relief is another design option where the mate and remaining section permit it. Identify the changed feature and preserve the mating envelope. If the corner locates another component, review that mate before changing the radius. Compare one defined alternative at a time so the price difference can be traced to the design change.

Separate fixed enclosure interfaces from negotiable geometry
FeatureKeep fixed where function requires itAlternative worth reviewing
Lid rimRegister, sealing contact and fastening relationship.Change a clearance corner outside the working seal or register.
Tall cavity wallMinimum space for the board and connectors.Add local support or shorten an unsupported span where the assembly permits.
Deep internal cornerMating component envelope and required contact.Increase permitted radius or add a designed relief.
Mounting bossWorking height, hole position and fastener engagement.Alter surrounding nonfunctional stock to improve support and access.

Ask for a marked model showing each proposed change. A general permission to simplify the cavity is too broad when a small step also locates the lid or supports a board. Price the accepted alternative against its own revision and preserve the original interface checks.

sections.title: A hole needs room for the tool and the fastener
sections.html:
A hole near a cavity wall may admit a small cutter while blocking the holder, deburring tool or gauge. A side port may require another holding orientation, with enough support to protect the thin wall and finished rim. The full surrounding geometry belongs in the review.

Usable thread depth differs from drilled depth

Blind threaded holes for lid screws need enough full thread and clearance to avoid bottoming. Show the usable thread depth, drilled depth and material left beneath the hole in section, especially near a thin floor or pocket. Define where drilling and threading must stop.

Installation brings another clearance check. The screw head, counterbore, connector body and driver can compete for room around the same rim. Through holes also need an accepted exit edge, which may become hard to reach once other features are completed.

Access from opposite sides can simplify a deep feature, while splitting the housing introduces another locating and sealing joint. That trade-off should be reviewed at assembly level. Protected fixture-contact faces and any proposed temporary stock belong in the agreed manufacturing route.

sections.title: Evaluate the lid and bores after the complete route
sections.html:
Dimensions after anodizing need to preserve the precision bore and controlled sealing rim as well as the exterior appearance. CNC enclosure masking should identify the local interfaces whose accepted surface differs from the main treatment. The final limits need to apply in the specified treated or masked condition. The material and finish guide covers the general process; the masking guide follows local bores, threads and contact surfaces.

A color reference controls appearance; flatness and position callouts require measurements. Normal cutter marks may be acceptable in a clearance cavity while the sealing rim has a separate texture requirement.

Measurement access matters early. A probe, bore gauge and height measurement do not reach every recess in the same way. A thin housing also needs its support or restraint condition defined where it affects the result. Any environmental sealing or ingress-protection requirement needs a separately agreed test and limit.

If the lid binds after finishing

Enclosure fit inspection should compare the finished lid register and housing opening in the same specified condition. Thin wall measurement also needs the agreed support or restraint before a bowed rim is treated as a size problem. Check the treated or masked surfaces, corner clearances and entry chamfers, then inspect the seating-face condition. A burr, local treatment edge or bowed rim calls for a different correction from an undersized opening.

Measure the agreed free or restrained state before removing material. Loosening the drawing limits to fit one assembled sample can conceal an unresolved route or tolerance-stack problem. Any accepted rework should identify the surface changed, its final protection and the checks repeated on the lid and housing.

sections.title: Enclosure drawings and sections to send for quotation
sections.html:
A CNC enclosure RFQ needs an aluminum housing specification that identifies where the lid, board and connectors locate. Mark the sections that are fixed and those open to a design proposal. Use a common revision for the model and drawing, and identify which file controls if they differ.

That package should include material and stock condition, the datums and working fits, sections through deep pockets, allowed radii and usable thread depths. Treatment boundaries and appearance references complete the finished definition. Required dimensional records, separate assembly tests, quantity and destination then establish the quotation scope.

For a machined aluminum enclosure, unresolved decisions can remain visibly marked during review. A supplier can discuss access and support around those constraints; the released revision records the approved result.

how-to-specify-fits-and-runout-on-turned.seoTitle: Fits and runout on turned shafts and sleeves
how-to-specify-fits-and-runout-on-turned.heading: Fits and runout on turned shafts and sleeves
how-to-specify-fits-and-runout-on-turned.description: Define shaft and sleeve fits, working lengths, datums, circular and total runout, with measurement and finishing tied to the assembly.
how-to-specify-fits-and-runout-on-turned.intro: A shaft can meet its diameter limits yet fail the assembly because a shoulder is misplaced or a working surface runs out relative to the locating axis. Specify shaft fits and runout from the working interfaces, with separate requirements for size, axial location and form.
how-to-specify-fits-and-runout-on-turned.summary: Size, shoulder location and surface variation relative to the working axis.
how-to-specify-fits-and-runout-on-turned.reader_question: Which fit and geometric controls make a turned part assemble and run as intended?

sections.title: Identify what each diameter and shoulder does
sections.html:
A bearing seat, seal track and removable coupling can occupy the same shaft. Their working lengths and mating conditions differ, so one blanket tolerance across the profile can add work while leaving the most important interface poorly described.

Shaft shoulder position and bearing seat length should follow the installed mating component. For each fitted region, show that component, the axial extent of the fit and any lead-in needed for assembly. A shoulder sets an axial stop, but the corner transition must also clear the mating component. A section through the installed parts makes those relationships visible.

The flanged turned reference has a central bore, stepped diameters and a face; the assembly determines which feature locates it. A sleeve likewise needs a defined relationship between its inner and outer surfaces as well as size limits. Specify grade, hardness where required and final finish beside that working geometry.

sections.title: Separate size from form and from the datum relationship
sections.html:
Diameter limits control permitted size. A shoulder dimension controls axial location. Circular runout evaluates surface variation at circular sections around the specified datum axis; total runout addresses the requirement over the controlled extent. The selected drawing standard determines the full meaning of each callout.

Hexagon's circular-runout documentation describes evaluation around a datum axis. Circular runout inspection must establish the specified datum reference in a way that represents the drawing. Total runout measurement also needs coverage over the controlled extent; a rotating part and an indicator alone do not describe either procedure.

When cylindricity answers a different question

The cylindricity vs runout distinction determines whether the result concerns surface form alone or a relationship to a datum. Datum axis establishment belongs to the runout procedure; cylindricity controls the cylindrical surface itself without a datum reference. A surface can have an acceptable form yet sit incorrectly relative to the axis that locates the assembly.

Hexagon's coordinate-metrology guide describes these different controls. The designer selects the required relationship; the supplier reviews a practical method and coverage. A roundness reading or a few diameter readings cannot replace a specified runout result, and a software alignment using a different reference may answer a different question.

Match the measurement to the shaft requirement
CharacteristicCoverage to establishQuestion to resolve before comparing results
DiameterThe specified fitted region and appropriate sections or measurements.Were both teams checking the same working length and final state?
FormSurface coverage needed for the selected control.Can the chosen points or traces detect the relevant shape variation?
Circular runoutStated sections referenced to the required datum axis.How was that axis established and supported?
Total runoutThe controlled surface extent relative to the datum axis.Does the procedure cover the full requirement?

A diameter reading near the entrance of a sleeve may miss variation deeper in its working bore. Similarly, turning a shaft between convenient centres can establish a different reference from the fitted journals named on the drawing. Record the locating contacts and evaluated region with the result.

sections.title: Choose clearance from the mating limits and service
sections.html:
A shaft and hole fit depends on the limits of both components. Shaft fit tolerances should express the selected clearance, transition or interference arrangement over the required working region. A clearance fit leaves space between the mating sizes over their specified limits. A transition fit can produce clearance or interference, while an interference fit is selected for the intended overlap. Which arrangement suits a bearing, sliding sleeve or coupling depends on assembly, load, movement and the operating condition.

For an illustrative room-temperature size calculation, assume a bore of 20.020 to 20.040 mm and a shaft of 20.000 to 20.010 mm. The minimum diametral clearance is 20.020 - 20.010 = 0.010 mm; the maximum diametral clearance is 20.040 - 20.000 = 0.040 mm. These assumed limits demonstrate the arithmetic only. They are not a recommended bearing or sliding fit, and they do not include form, temperature or surface effects.

SKF's bearing guidance considers rotation, load, temperature differences and shaft or housing construction. The actual bearing arrangement needs its corresponding guidance and engineering selection. Once selected, the drawing also needs the working length and clearance around the seating shoulder.

A fit designation still needs a nominal size

In an ISO limits-and-fits designation such as H7/g6, uppercase H7 identifies the hole zone and grade, while lowercase g6 identifies the shaft zone and grade. The numeric limits depend on the nominal diameter and the applicable standard. Copying the same designation from another shaft without checking size and duty leaves the actual clearance unresolved.

Identify the actual bearing before releasing the fit. Apply the bearing maker's design recommendations, SKF's installation guidance and the chosen drawing standard to that arrangement.

sections.title: Keep flats and cross-holes related to the working axis
sections.html:
Milled flat orientation may matter when the flat transmits torque or locates a clamp. Cross-hole position similarly needs to follow the working axis and any reference that establishes the installed direction. A cross-hole may set the orientation of a pin or fluid connection. Their depth and location need references to the turned features that locate the part in service.

Whether turning and milling share a machine or use separate setups, the flat or cross-hole must retain its specified relationship to the turned locating features. The inspection plan should evaluate that relationship from the drawing datums.

Long shafts need support that does not hide an unacceptable free-state shape. Thin sleeves can move under holding or measuring force. A deep bore also needs an approach for cutting, deburring and measurement at the required depth. The drawing should state the shape or restraint condition that matters, while the route review resolves support and access around it.

sections.title: Record the surface in the condition that enters service
sections.html:
Plating or anodizing can affect a fitted diameter; electropolishing can alter the material surface. The final drawing should identify which limits apply after the complete route, which regions are masked and whether any approved sizing follows treatment. Surface roughness and the condition of seal tracks or thread entries need their own acceptance requirements.

Keep the size result beside the runout result

Shaft surface finish needs to remain identifiable beside the size and geometric results for each journal. For a sleeve, bore measurement depth and the evaluated sections must likewise describe the working region, final state and specified datums. Choose the measurement method, coverage and sampling for each control, including support where a slender or thin part can move.

The material and finish guide follows the effect of treatment on interfaces. For threads and fluid connections, the thread and seal guide addresses the separate connection definition.

When two runout readings disagree

Compare each runout measurement setup using the same part, revision and finished state. For thin sleeve inspection, reproduce the support and contact conditions without deforming the measured feature. Compare datum establishment, support locations, measurement sections and contact method. Check whether either setup restrains a slender shaft or thin sleeve. A difference in support can change the observed result even when both teams use an indicator.

Keep the original readings and setup descriptions while the method is reconciled. If an agreed method changes the release decision, attach that method to the acceptance record. Reworking the diameter before understanding the disagreement can affect a fit that already met its own limits.

sections.title: Release the mating relationship with the part drawing
sections.html:
Name the mating components and working lengths on the drawing, with size limits, shoulder locations, datums and local surface requirements. Keep model and drawing units and revisions consistent. Specify material condition, final treatment and protected regions.

The quotation also needs quantity, destination, the required dimensional report and any first-article or sampling plan. An assembly trial should identify its components and setup; it supplies evidence for those recorded checks. The turning review can then address holding, secondary work and measurement against the actual part.

choosing-thread-and-seal-requirements-fo.seoTitle: Threads and seals for custom machined fittings
choosing-thread-and-seal-requirements-fo.heading: Threads and seals for custom machined fittings
choosing-thread-and-seal-requirements-fo.description: Define thread identity, sealing geometry, passage intersections, gauging and separate leakage or pressure tests for a custom fitting.
choosing-thread-and-seal-requirements-fo.intro: Machined fitting thread and seal requirements identify how each end connects and where the fluid seal forms. A familiar thread size does not settle the seal, passage or assembled test. Work from the actual mating ports and selected seal, then carry those interfaces through machining, treatment and inspection.
choosing-thread-and-seal-requirements-fo.summary: Thread identity, sealing contact and the scope of component or assembly checks.
choosing-thread-and-seal-requirements-fo.reader_question: What must I define so a custom fitting connects, seals and can be accepted?

sections.title: Identify both ends completely
sections.html:
Port thread identification should establish pitch, thread form, taper and the actual mating connection. A fitting thread specification must then retain that complete definition; a familiar-looking replacement adapter can differ in any of those details. Each end needs its complete designation, including the applicable standard, size and required class or other acceptance details. The connection also needs its engagement length, orientation where relevant and mating reference.

Swagelok's thread and end-connection identification guide can help identify a sample connection. Record sample measurements separately from the approved production specification; similar-looking threads are not an agreed substitution.

The quotation should distinguish a machined body from an assembled connection. Identify the seals, plugs, inserts and other hardware, with part references and responsibility for supplying each item. Use the CNC turning review to discuss the body's locating features and any secondary machining.

sections.title: The sealing contact and its mating geometry
sections.html:
The sealing contact may be in the threads, at a gasket face, around an O-ring or at another defined seat. The connection design determines which geometry controls it. A thread result alone cannot establish that a separate seat has the correct profile, texture or relationship to the port.

Swagelok's discussion of small-bore fitting types explains why end connections use different sealing arrangements. The selected design needs the corresponding mating component and installation requirements, not a generic assumption taken from the outside shape.

Use a section through the installed seal

O-ring groove design should follow the selected seal in its installed condition. Show the supported contact region, adjacent chamfers and controlling references in section, with sealing surface finish specified on the actual working land. The selected groove dimensions belong with that seal definition; a gasket seat needs its own face geometry and texture. Burrs, treatment edges or a corner transition can disturb the seal contact even when the thread gauges correctly.

Select the seal before releasing its groove

Seal material compatibility needs the seal size, compound and application, including the relevant fluid, temperature and pressure conditions. Machined fitting assembly scope should also identify whether that selected seal and mating hardware are supplied. An existing groove can supply measurements for investigation, but its geometry alone does not establish the intended elastomer or allowable compression.

The Parker handbook treats seal materials and gland geometry by application. Use the selected design to define groove width, depth, supporting faces, assembly gap and entry geometry. The finished dimensions need to account for the mating hardware and treatment so the approved seal reaches its intended installed state.

Where the customer selects and installs the seals and mating hardware, retain their approved references with the body drawing so a later substitute can be assessed against the same gland definition.

sections.title: Keep NPT, BSPT and metric connection details distinct
sections.html:
To compare NPT vs BSP threads, identify the exact family and end connection. Compare parallel vs tapered threads by their geometry, and specify the sealing arrangement separately. A metric thread also leaves the sealing arrangement to be defined. The drawing should retain the selected family and complete designation through quotation, machining and final gauging.

For a replacement sample, use the Swagelok thread and end-connection guide to identify the family and complete designation before approving it for the custom assembly.

A proposed change should be reviewed with the mating port and seal as a connection. If plating or another treatment follows machining, include the final engagement and thread acceptance condition in that review. Gauges and the inspection method should match the specified finished connection.

Identify the thread and then the sealing connection
FamilyDistinction to verifyDefinition still needed
NPTTapered pipe thread with a 60° form under the specified standard.Complete size, engagement, gauge requirements and assembly sealing method.
BSPTTapered pipe-thread system with a 55° profile.Exact male/female designations and the specified mating connection.
BSPPParallel pipe thread with a 55° profile.The connection's separate seat, washer, O-ring or other sealing arrangement.
MetricNominal diameter, pitch, form and class of the specified thread.How this port connection seals and locates.

The Swagelok identification guide separates thread standards from end-connection standards. BSP thread identification needs more than pitch because some nominal sizes have similar pitches across families. Thread engagement length and the complete mating connection must also be established before approving a replacement. A replacement sample needs a confirmed connection specification before its measurements become manufacturing instructions.

sections.title: The internal intersection deserves its own drawing view
sections.html:
Cross-hole deburring must address the intersection inside the fitting, where a clean-looking entrance can conceal a burr. Internal passage cleanliness needs its own acceptance basis where debris would affect the connected equipment. Sections should show passage diameters, depths, intersections and blind terminations. The drawing needs to identify where a loose burr, restricted passage or damaged edge would affect assembly or flow.

That internal geometry must be reachable for cutting, deburring and the agreed check. A thin wall beside a thread, deep recess or blind intersection can limit the route. Any permitted access opening or plug should appear in the supplied component definition rather than becoming an informal manufacturing change.

Specify the material grade, finish and handling needed to preserve the accepted seal and passage condition through delivery.

sections.title: Thread acceptance and leakage testing answer different questions
sections.html:
Thread gauge inspection addresses the specified thread, while dimensional checks address the bore, seat and datum relationships. A machined fitting leak test or a specified pressure test needs an assembled configuration, procedure, medium, conditions and acceptance limit. Its inclusion and reporting responsibility need to be agreed in the quotation.

Name the configuration that was tested

The body revision, mating port, seals and assembly method belong with the result. A successful trial of one recorded configuration does not establish an unreviewed replacement seal or later coating route. Those changes need the affected checks reviewed before approval is repeated.

Before comparing unit prices, check whether each offer covers a gauged body only or also hardware, assembly and a defined leak test.

Leak-test conditions to record

Leak test acceptance criteria need the medium, pressure or differential, stabilization and measurement periods, detection method and limit with units. Record the fitting test configuration alongside those conditions. Identify plugged ports, seals, mating hardware and the assembly procedure used. Gas and liquid results from different configurations are separate evidence.

For a supplied body only, the dimensional record can include the specified thread and sealing-seat checks. An assembly test performed later should retain that body's identity and revision. A pressure value written on an inquiry, without a method or acceptance criterion, leaves the required test undefined.

sections.title: A complete connection definition makes the RFQ usable
sections.html:
The current drawing and model should identify each end connection, the selected material and condition, seal arrangement, internal passages and treatment boundaries. A replacement sample can accompany the package with its observations kept distinct from confirmed specifications.

Required gauges, dimensional records, material traceability and any separate tests complete acceptance. The order also needs body or assembly scope, included hardware, quantity, identification and destination. The RFQ checklist organizes those items; the connection details should remain on the controlled drawing or specification so assembly and receiving inspection use the approved definition.

which-aluminum-features-need-masking-bef.seoTitle: Which aluminum features need masking before anodizing?
which-aluminum-features-need-masking-bef.heading: Which aluminum features need masking before anodizing?
which-aluminum-features-need-masking-bef.description: Compare masking, machining allowances and approved sizing after anodizing for bores, threads, seals and electrical contacts.
which-aluminum-features-need-masking-bef.intro: Masking is useful when a local surface needs a different condition from the rest of an anodized part. A locating bore may need to keep its machined size; a contact pad may need a specified electrical interface. The decision also has to preserve protection and define the boundary at the chamfer, shoulder or seal beside it.
which-aluminum-features-need-masking-bef.summary: Choose a route for each working feature and show where its treatment ends.
which-aluminum-features-need-masking-bef.reader_question: Which features should remain outside anodizing, and how do I define the resulting fit and protection?

sections.title: Identify the surface that must keep its function
sections.html:
Anodizing masking requirements should follow the local interface function. Masking fitted bores calls for a different review from protecting a seal region, threaded connection or electrical contact. A clearance opening can tolerate a condition that a locating band or current-carrying pad cannot.

A bore's lead-in chamfer, adjacent shoulder and intersecting passage can place a treatment edge inside the mating interface. Show which regions receive anodizing and which stay outside the main treatment in a section view.

The untreated region also needs an accepted service condition. Preserving a fit by masking is only suitable if the resulting exposed surface and any separate protection meet the assembly's environment and contact requirements.

Turn a coloured treatment map into local drawing requirements
RegionBoundary to defineCompleted-state check
Locating boreCylindrical length, mouth chamfer and adjoining shoulder.Final fit and the stated condition of each region.
Blind threaded holeUsable thread, entrance and any internal masking boundary.Required final gauging and the specified protection.
Grounding padContact area and its relationship to nearby fasteners or edges.Permitted surface condition and any separately agreed electrical check.
Seal trackThe contact region and a transition kept clear of its working path.Local surface and dimensional requirements.

For masking blind threads, define the required usable thread and entrance condition. When anodizing contact pads, identify the working region and its required surface condition. The processor can then choose plugs or tapes to achieve those results. The engineering definition should state the required result and any mandatory constraints, with the processor confirming an achievable boundary. A plug selected by nominal hole size alone leaves the chamfer and shoulder outcome unresolved.

sections.title: Use the final size to review the allowance
sections.html:
An anodized bore tolerance must describe the completed working surface. Review anodizing coating growth, preparation and process variation before selecting a machining allowance for a bore that must retain its treatment. The allowance needs to be reviewed for that bore; a nominal coating thickness does not provide the complete answer.

NASA/JSC's anodizing specification discusses dimensional change and hard-anodizing coverage limits in small or deep internal features. Check coverage inside the bore as well as its final fit; an exterior coating result does not establish either.

Suppose, purely as an illustration, a process is assumed to add 8 micrometres outward on each side of a coated bore. The opening would reduce by about 16 micrometres. The actual machining allowance must also account for preparation, variation and the required final limits. This assumed value gives no production allowance for an unspecified process.

Where the route uses measurements at more than one stage, label them accordingly. An intermediate bore result can control machining; final acceptance must address the completed condition required by the drawing.

sections.title: Compare three routes for the same fitted bore
sections.html:
The routes leave different working surfaces

RouteWhy it may fit the designWhat needs approval
Mask the bore before anodizingThe identified region retains its machined surface outside the main treatment.Final size, masking boundary and protection of that region.
Machine an allowance and accept the treated boreThe working surface retains the selected treatment.Process-specific allowance, achievable coverage and final dimensional checks.
Anodize, then perform an approved sizing operationA later operation establishes the final fitted size.Removed coating, exposed region and final protection or surface requirement.

A reamed bore and a masked bore can both expose base material, but they reach that condition by different sequences. The approved route needs to preserve the required chamfer and shoulder condition as well as the diameter. The finishing supplier should review the achievable boundary before release.

Machining after anodizing needs approval for any coating removed or base material exposed. Final thread gauging must then follow the specified designation, usable engagement and accepted processing sequence. Electrical contacts similarly need the specified contact area and any separately required resistance or bonding test. A seal region needs the complete mating arrangement so the mask edge stays clear of its working contact.

sections.title: Plan the process contact and inspect the boundary
sections.html:
Anodizing rack marks arise from the electrical contact needed during processing. The allowed contact region must be considered alongside the anodized appearance sample and the functional surfaces. A convenient racking point can be unacceptable on a visible panel, seal face or fitted surface. The drawing should identify allowed contact locations or clearly prohibited regions for processor review.

The appearance reference should represent the specified alloy and preparation. Color, gloss and permitted marks need agreed viewing conditions. A change to the alloy, preparation or processor may require a review of the earlier sample approval and the process used to achieve the final dimensions.

Boundary and size checks after mask removal

The accepted result includes the untreated bore length, chamfer, shoulder and any intersecting opening defined by the drawing. Masking boundary inspection and final size checks answer different questions. Record the measurement locations and results for hard anodizing thickness separately from the boundary and bore-size checks.

Prepare the grade and process records described in the material and finish guide against the same production revision as the local treatment details.

Keep anodizing sealing distinct from assembly sealing

The anodizing sealing process treats the anodic coating. Assembly leak testing evaluates a different requirement: a sealed anodized surface alone supplies no leakage result for the housing joint. An enclosure or fitting still needs its own gasket or O-ring definition and any specified assembly test.

NASA/JSC PRC-5006 treats sealing and local protection within its anodizing process requirements. It also discusses protection of masked holes. Apply the specification selected for the actual order and obtain approval for the bare or separately protected regions it leaves.

After mask removal, inspect the named boundary and the final working dimensions. If the treatment extends onto a protected land or stops short of a required area, record the affected feature before touching up or removing material. The approved disposition needs to preserve both the fit and the required local protection.

sections.title: Release a treatment map that can be inspected
sections.html:
An anodizing drawing specification needs named requirements behind each treated or masked region. Masked surface protection must be included where the exposed region needs a separate accepted condition; a colored screenshot alone leaves that requirement open. The drawing or attached specification should identify the grade and condition, treatment type and applicable revision, required thickness, preparation and appearance reference.

For each fitted, threaded, sealing or contact region, include the boundary view, final size and required surface condition. Any separate protection, permitted rack marks and final inspection records belong in the same package. Changes to boundaries or the finishing route need an identified approver.

Send that definition with the aluminum machining inquiry. An unresolved surface can remain marked as an open decision during quotation; the approved treatment map completes the manufacturing release.

specifying-a-billet-intake-manifold-for-.seoTitle: Specifying a billet intake manifold for machining
specifying-a-billet-intake-manifold-for-.heading: Specifying a billet intake manifold for machining
specifying-a-billet-intake-manifold-for-.description: Define billet intake manifold ports, runners, flange relationships and split joints, with component supply, fitment and tests stated separately.
specifying-a-billet-intake-manifold-for-.intro: Billet intake manifold machining needs controlled internal passages and the interfaces that connect them to the head, throttle and seals. The machining review then has to establish access to those surfaces and any joints used to close them. A complete-looking outside model leaves these questions open unless the mating definitions and supplied components accompany it.
specifying-a-billet-intake-manifold-for-.summary: Mating geometry, internal access and the evidence needed for the supplied components.
specifying-a-billet-intake-manifold-for-.reader_question: What files and acceptance requirements make a custom billet manifold ready for a machining review?

sections.title: Use the actual head, throttle and seal interfaces
sections.html:
Intake manifold fitment requires the runner openings of a billet intake manifold to meet their intended ports in the assembled position. The flange faces, mounting pattern and selected seals establish that relationship, while injector locations and auxiliary connections add their own hardware and orientation requirements.

For the interfaces shown in the multi-runner manifold reference, supply the controlling head, throttle, injector and bracket drawings or approved mating components relevant to the design.

Holley's manifold technical support addresses head, port, gasket and installed-clearance questions for its products. Check those relationships on the actual custom assembly; another product's instructions do not establish its fitment.

An engine name leaves the revision unresolved

A vehicle or engine name does not identify the port positions or version of every mating part. Record the identity and purpose of any physical component used in a fit trial. Its approval covers that configuration, not an unreviewed variant.

Record the installed configuration before port matching

Intake manifold port matching needs the actual head definition, selected gasket or seal and intended mounting arrangement. The throttle body flange also needs its controlled opening, mounting pattern and installed orientation. If the trial uses physical components, record their identity, revision and any known modification. A previously surfaced head or changed port height can alter the mating relationship.

Check the installed envelope with injector connectors, fuel-rail hardware, throttle actuation and nearby brackets where they belong to the design. A port-aligned model can still leave insufficient room for a connector, fastener tool or moving linkage. The released assembly should show the relevant clearance throughout the required movement.

sections.title: Choose the construction around internal access and joints
sections.html:
The intake manifold CAD model needs complete intake runner geometry, including sections through transitions, recessed ports and blind intersections. Regions whose profile or texture controls the design should be identified, along with any geometry open to an access-related change.

A one-piece design needs a practical cutting and inspection approach through its openings. Splitting the runners or chamber can expose more surfaces before closure, while adding a joint that must locate, seal and remain accessible for assembly. The comparison therefore includes the new mating geometry and hardware as well as machining access.

A split intake manifold needs internal passage alignment as well as joint retention. Fasteners can retain the pieces while a register, dowel or other selected feature establishes the required alignment. The drawing needs to control any allowed step across the internal passage and provide support for the seal around it. Bolt access and nearby wall thickness belong in the same section review.

Port matching needs the transition as well as the opening

A gasket outline can help describe the sealing envelope but may leave the head-port position, flange thickness and runner transition unresolved. The controlled mating model or drawing should establish those relationships. The manifold and chamber files also need a common revision basis so matching names do not conceal incompatible surfaces.

An instruction to make the passages smooth needs a defined region and measurable surface requirement if it will govern acceptance. Internal appearance alone establishes no flow or operating-performance result. Some checks must be planned while a split component is still open.

Plan the checks while each manifold surface remains accessible
StageGeometry to establishRecord before proceeding
Open machined piecesRunner profile, local texture, internal intersections and specified cleanliness.Results for the required accessible regions.
Joint preparationRegisters or dowels, seal land and permitted passage mismatch.The mating revision and local dimensional checks.
Assembly, if includedHardware, seal placement, clearances and the approved assembly procedure.The actual assembled configuration and included components.
Final acceptanceRemaining geometry and any separately specified test.Completed checks, outstanding items and release authority.

Where a joint step controls acceptance, specify its limit and measurement references. The seal-interface review covers auxiliary fluid ports that use their own threaded connection or gland.

sections.title: Interface definitions and acceptance checks
sections.html:
InterfaceControlling definitionAcceptance scope
Head flange and runnersPort profile, positions, mounting references and seal.Specified position, face geometry and local surface results.
Throttle connectionMating opening, pattern, orientation and envelope.Fit, clearance and seal-interface checks.
Injector or auxiliary portApproved hardware, connection and retention details.Dimensions plus any separately agreed functional check.
Split jointLocating features, fasteners and sealing arrangement.Alignment, surface and assembled requirements.
Internal passageComplete profile and any local texture requirements.Defined checks at a stage where the surface is accessible.

Each machined component needs its material and condition. The component list must identify whether inserts, seals and fasteners are included and who supplies them. The effect of treatment on final fits needs to be resolved before the machining and inspection sequence is approved.

The intake manifold sealing face and injector port position need to remain related to the installed mating references. The full outside envelope also matters to holding and tool access. Protected faces, additional orientations or proposed temporary stock should be discussed against the complete component geometry.

sections.title: A component order and a validated assembly have different deliverables
sections.html:
List the supplied manifold components and hardware in the quotation, identifying the runners, chamber, flanges and other pieces being delivered. Then define the intake manifold assembly scope: who joins those pieces, what assembly work is included and whether they arrive open or assembled.

Dimensional inspection records geometry. A fit trial uses named mating components or controlled equivalents. Leakage testing needs a configuration, procedure, conditions and limit. A flow or operating-performance requirement needs its own suitable plan and responsible party. Billet construction and an accepted dimensional report establish no particular power or flow improvement.

A prototype approval should retain the actual configuration, revision, completed checks and accepted exceptions. A later change to a throttle, seal or runner requires the affected acceptance to be reviewed. LZZ's aluminum machining review focuses on the controlled components and agreed order scope; any required joining or external test should be identified in the initial inquiry.

Define the operating test separately from the machining release

An intake manifold leak test using vacuum needs the differential, plugged openings, installed seals, method, stabilization period and permitted leakage stated with units. Choose a separate procedure and acceptance basis for manifold flow testing and for any pressure test through the responsible design and test authority.

Keep the machined-component checks available even when a later assembly test is performed elsewhere. If the prototype uses temporary plugs or hardware, record them so the result can be interpreted against the intended delivered configuration.

sections.title: Release the configuration the next order should repeat
sections.html:
The released models and drawings should cover every supplied component, its mating references and seals. Material condition, final treatment and the relevant assembly clearances belong with the internal profile and local surface requirements. For any open design decision, name the person responsible for resolving it before production release.

The order also needs component or assembly scope, included hardware, joining responsibility, quantity and the dimensional records. Fitment, leakage and performance checks should each have their own agreed acceptance and responsibility where required.

Manifold prototype approval and repeat manifold orders should retain the accepted mating components and completed results with the sample approval record. Cite that configuration on the repeat order and identify any test still awaiting completion.
